attributes.action: Introduce routine tongue-tie screening for all newborn babies in Scotland.
attributes.additional_details: Tongue-tie can affect newborn babies by causing breastfeeding and bottle-feeding difficulties, poor weight gain, prolonged feeds, pain during breastfeeding and unnecessary distress for families. Access to NHS assessment and treatment varies across Scotland, creating a postcode lottery. We call on the Scottish Government to introduce routine newborn tongue-tie assessments and ensure timely NHS treatment, including frenotomy where clinically appropriate.
attributes.background: the Scottish Government to introduce routine tongue-tie (ankyloglossia) screening for all newborn babies in NHS Scotland. Babies with a clinically significant tongue-tie that is affecting feeding should receive prompt assessment and treatment, including frenotomy where appropriate.

rejection.details:
Your petition is about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/

You may also wish to contact your local council and MSP who represent you about this issue. 

You can find the name of your local council and how to contact them here: https://www.mygov.scot/find-your-local-council

You can find the name of your local MSP and how to contact them here: https://www.parliament.scot/msps
